findings.classification: conditional source-backed identity/producer-consumer relationship; actual supported duplicate reachability and canonical count remain open
findings.first_contract: When HumanoidRig caching encounters multiple HumanoidBone entries with the same owner and BoneRole, it retains the minimum entity and warns. The report collector queries all owned reportable HumanoidBone entries, converts each into (role,sample), and FromIterator builds a BTreeMap keyed by role, dropping duplicate multiplicity. It does not compare retained query entity identity with the rig cache.
findings.conditional_reasoning: If an admissible scene contains two reportable bones with the same owner and role, and the collection retains the higher entity while the rig retained the lower, report observation and the rig-selected role can refer to different source transforms. The project declares nightly-2026-07-13; its installed std source implements stable key sorting then keeps the last duplicate. For this implementation a later query position for the higher entity would produce that relationship. The public BTreeMap FromIterator documentation promises only that all but one duplicate value is dropped; the exact last-entry behavior is source-path/toolchain-implementation-qualified, not a universal API guarantee. No source here establishes actual query order, compiler used in any run, valid duplicate-producing asset/scene, differing transform, capture, rendered output, or overall validation success.
findings.safeguards: Normal scene loader skips actors already marked AnimationRigAttached; that narrows but does not prove a unique role inside every admitted scene. Required-frame completion checks presence of all 17 mapped roles, not role multiplicity. Repeated-view comparison checks keys and sample changes but the inspected bodies do not guarantee stable selection of the same rig-authoritative entity. Other gates remain independent.

thirteen_lens_dispositions.disposition: Report keys serialize only for mapped roles; map construction alone does not establish required-role completeness, unique producer or finite native transform.
Frame/plan match and all 17 required keys are a separate report-level contract; candidate duplicate selection relates collection to the independently cached rig owner.
Report intentionally preserves lexical labels for iteration, folds and ties; the older P17 equal-key zipped comparator and current lookup have separate source histories.
BoneRole derives ordering; CapturedBones has custom iteration and serialization to preserve report-label order and reject unmapped roles, so no automatic derive replacement is established.
27 semantic rig roles and 17 report labels represent distinct scopes; absence/unmapped role has an explicit Option at the reporting adapter.
CapturedBones keys use existing BoneRole; labels are boundary representation, not a second gameplay rig enum.
The current repeated delta and numerical shortcut were separately assessed earlier; incomplete finite checks or duplicate collection cannot be declared safe from role typing alone.
Roster count and collection order are structural. Existing current repeat thresholds have separate numerical evidence; preserve their intended tolerances.
Museum IDs are catalog-facing identifiers and report labels are external report names; lookup/asset admission and stable label policy stay open.
Authenticated rig identities produce HumanoidBone owner/role, then query samples propagate into a report map; multiplicity/authority remains conditional.
Current rig chooses lowest entity per duplicate while report maps same-role samples through independent collection. Divergence requires an admitted duplicate and qualifying query order.
Capture subset, complete semantic rig vocabulary, and authored rig joint identity are separate meaningful layers; no blanket merge or expansion.
Canonical entity selection and duplicate admission remain rig/capture boundary questions, with earlier same-role queue links preserved for central reconciliation.
